newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine $2.3 bln wage debt stability threat-expert.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine $2.3 bln wage debt stability threat-expert.

text.p: Ukraine's $2.31 billion wage debt to doctors, teachers and workers posed a threat to the country's stability if not checked, an economic expert told a meeting of politicians and economists on Wednesday.
"This is one of the major problems of Ukraine's economic security and stability," said Olexander Razumkov, chief of the Ukrainian Centre for Economic and Political Research.
Razumkov quoted a recent survey, carried out by the Ukrainian Centre for Economic and Political Research, which stated 59 percent of Ukrainians' pay was late by two to five months.
"You can imagine the mood of the people living under these conditions," he said.
The government owes wages to coal miners, government employees and employees of state-run enterprises, and also holds a $600,000 debt to pensioners.
Demands for unpaid wages were behind the nation-wide "Day of Action" strike last week in which some 85,000 people took part.
High government officials recently blamed directors of state-run enterprises for holding back wages, which average between $80 and $90 a month compared to pensions averaging $30 per month.
